raw_response:
I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for me to use my 12 mu, my well water, and the labor my family can still put together even with some people working off-farm. I am old and I have farmed a long time, so I do not want to spread myself too thin with too much cotton, which takes more picking and closer watching. I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2 mu in cotton because I already know how to manage it and I still want some cash crop income. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps me get stable emergence and yield, and I will stay with moderate fertilizer rates rather than chasing the very highest output. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate at the key times instead of depending only on rainfall. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and fits the way I manage land now. I will spray pesticides only as much as needed to keep labor and cost under control while protecting yield.
